name: Estimate remaining daylight with your hand
blurb: The fastest useful field trick there is: each finger between the sun and the horizon is roughly 15 minutes of daylight. Learn it once, use it forever.
steps: Extend your arm fully and turn your hand sideways, palm towards you, little finger resting on the horizon.
Count the fingers that fit between the horizon and the bottom of the sun, stacking hands if needed.
Each finger is about 15 minutes, so a full hand is roughly an hour.
Calibrate against sunset time for your location on a few clear evenings and adjust for your own hand size.
Learn to add roughly 30 minutes of usable twilight after the sun touches the horizon at mid-latitudes.
Use it to make real decisions: turn-around times, when to start making camp.
tips: Never look directly at the sun. Sight just below it.
The estimate is worst near the poles and in mountains, where the horizon is high and the sun sets behind terrain.
proof: Three evenings running, your estimate lands within 15 minutes of actual sunset.
